sections.title: Warm-up
sections.lede: Read aloud and find the person who receives something.
sections.prompt: Say these sentences aloud. Each one has two objects: a thing and a person.
items: Ich gebe dem Kind einen Apfel.
Sie schenkt ihrer Schwester ein Buch.

sections.title: Learning objectives
sections.lede: By the end of this lesson you will be able to do these things.

sections.title: The big picture
sections.lede: Two objects, two cases: who receives, and what is given.

blocks.text: Many everyday verbs can take two objects. The thing that is given, shown or explained is the direct object and stands in the accusative. The person who receives it is the indirect object and stands in the dative. German marks the difference on the article, not on the noun.
Ich gebe dem Kind einen Apfel.
blocks.en: I give the child an apple.

items: Ask Wen oder was? for the accusative: einen Apfel.
Ask Wem? for the dative: dem Kind.
Verbs with two objects include geben, schenken, zeigen, bringen, schicken, erklären, empfehlen and leihen.
With two nouns, the dative comes first: dem Kind einen Apfel.

blocks.title: One case at a time
blocks.text: Find the person first, then the thing. Ich gebe — wem? dem Kind — was? einen Apfel. This order of questions prevents most article mistakes.

sections.title: Rules & patterns
sections.lede: The articles and the word order do most of the work.

rows: Ich gebe dem Kind einen Apfel.
Sie schenkt ihrer Schwester ein Buch.
Wir bringen den Nachbarn einen Kuchen.

items: Two nouns: dative before accusative — Ich gebe dem Kind den Apfel.
One pronoun and one noun: the pronoun comes first — Ich gebe ihn dem Kind.
Two pronouns: accusative before dative — Ich gebe es ihm.
A pronoun replaces a noun completely, so do not keep both: Ich gebe es ihm, not Ich gebe es dem Kind ihm.

rows: aus, bei, mit, nach, seit, von, zu

sections.title: Example sentences
sections.lede: Read each pair of objects aloud: person first, thing second.

items.de: Ich gebe dem Kind einen Apfel.
items.en: I give the child an apple.
items.note: dem Kind is dative, einen Apfel is accusative.

items.de: Sie schenkt ihrer Schwester ein Buch.
items.en: She gives her sister a book as a present.
items.note: ihrer Schwester is the feminine dative form.

items.de: Er zeigt mir den Weg zum Bahnhof.
items.en: He shows me the way to the station.
items.note: mir is the dative pronoun; den Weg is accusative.

items.de: Wir bringen den Nachbarn einen Kuchen.
items.en: We are bringing the neighbours a cake.
items.note: den Nachbarn is dative plural; the noun already ends in -n.

items.de: Kannst du es mir bitte erklären?
items.en: Can you explain it to me, please?
items.note: With two pronouns the accusative es comes before the dative mir.

sections.title: Pronunciation
sections.lede: The articles are short. Say them clearly enough to hear the case.

items.hint: Long e in the first syllable: GAY-ben. The second syllable is soft.
Start with “sh”, not a hard sk: SHEN-ken.
Long ä and stress on the second syllable: air-KLAY-ren.
Long o and a sharp s: GROHS-moo-ter. Do not voice the ß.
Said quickly it sounds like “eye-nem”. Keep both syllables so the dative stays audible.

blocks.text: German separates giving in general (geben) from giving a present (schenken). Both take a dative person and an accusative thing: Ich gebe dir den Schlüssel, but Ich schenke dir ein Buch.

Christmas presents are traditionally opened on Christmas Eve, Heiligabend, rather than on Christmas morning. Families often say Die Eltern schenken den Kindern Bücher — the same two-object pattern you have practised here.

sections.title: Dialogue in context
sections.lede: Two colleagues plan a farewell present.
sections.setting: In the office, planning a present for a colleague

lines.speaker: Sara
lines.de: Was schenken wir Herrn Berger eigentlich zum Abschied?
lines.en: What are we actually giving Mr Berger for his farewell?

lines.speaker: Tim
lines.de: Ich schenke ihm ein Buch. Er liest gern.
lines.en: I will give him a book. He likes reading.

lines.speaker: Sara
lines.de: Gute Idee. Und wer gibt ihm das Geschenk?
lines.en: Good idea. And who is giving him the present?

lines.speaker: Tim
lines.de: Wir geben es ihm am Freitag in der Mittagspause.
lines.en: We will give it to him on Friday during the lunch break.

lines.speaker: Sara
lines.de: Soll ich noch eine Karte besorgen?
lines.en: Should I get a card as well?

lines.speaker: Tim
lines.de: Ja, bitte. Schreib ihm ein paar nette Worte.
lines.en: Yes, please. Write him a few kind words.

lines.speaker: Sara
lines.de: Mache ich. Ich zeige dir den Text vorher.
lines.en: I will. I will show you the text beforehand.

sections.title: Grammar spotlight
sections.heading: Two objects: what goes where
sections.lede: Case decides the article; the type of object decides the order.

rows: Ich gebe dem Kind den Apfel.
I give the child the apple.
I give it to the child.

items: Pronouns come before nouns, whatever their case.
When both objects are pronouns, the accusative comes first.
When both objects are nouns, the dative comes first.
The same rules apply to schenken, zeigen, bringen, schicken, erklären, empfehlen and leihen.

blocks.title: Watch the dative plural
blocks.text: Dative plural articles are den, and the noun adds -n unless it already ends in -n or -s: den Kindern, den Nachbarn, but den Autos.

sections.tip: In a real conversation, say the person first and the thing second. Ich gebe dir das Buch is always safe, even when other orders are also correct.

sections.title: Choose the right answer
sections.lede: Choose the article or the word order that fits.

exercises.prompt: Complete: Ich gebe ___ Kind einen Apfel.
exercises.explanation: The child receives the apple, so it stands in the dative: dem Kind.

exercises.prompt: Complete: Sie schenkt ___ Schwester ein Buch.
exercises.explanation: die Schwester is feminine, and the dative of ihr is ihrer.
zeigen takes a dative person: er zeigt mir den Weg.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence has the natural order for two nouns?
options: Ich gebe einen Apfel dem Kind.
Ich gebe dem Kind einen Apfel.
Ich dem Kind gebe einen Apfel.
Ich gebe einen Apfel das Kind.
exercises.explanation: With two nouns, the dative person comes before the accusative thing.
With two pronouns the accusative es comes first, then the dative ihm.
für is an accusative preposition: für meinen Bruder. mit, nach and bei take the dative.

sections.title: Complete the sentence
sections.lede: Type the missing article or pronoun.

exercises.explanation: The person receiving is dative: dem Kind.
leihen takes a dative person: ihm.
für takes the accusative, and der Bruder becomes meinen Bruder.

sections.title: Listening
sections.lede: Listen twice, then answer from memory.
sections.speaker: In a gift shop

script.speaker: Verkäuferin
script.de: Guten Tag, kann ich Ihnen helfen?
script.en: Good day, can I help you?

script.speaker: Kunde
script.de: Ja, ich suche ein Geschenk für meinen Vater.
script.en: Yes, I am looking for a present for my father.

script.speaker: Verkäuferin
script.de: Wie wäre es mit diesem Buch?

script.speaker: Kunde
script.de: Er liest leider nicht viel. Haben Sie etwas für den Garten?
script.en: Unfortunately he does not read much. Do you have something for the garden?

script.speaker: Verkäuferin
script.de: Diese Werkzeuge sind sehr gut. Sie kosten zwanzig Euro.
script.en: These tools are very good. They cost twenty euros.

script.speaker: Kunde
script.de: Gut, ich nehme sie. Ich schenke sie ihm zum Geburtstag.
script.en: Good, I will take them. I will give them to him for his birthday.

questions.explanation: He says: Ich suche ein Geschenk für meinen Vater.

questions.prompt: Why does he not choose the book?
options: His father does not read much.
questions.explanation: He says: Er liest leider nicht viel.
He buys the tools: Ich nehme sie.

sections.title: Speaking
sections.lede: Describe a present you gave someone.
sections.prompt: Say three sentences about a present you gave. Use at least two sentences with both a dative person and an accusative thing.

model.de: Meine Schwester hatte letzte Woche Geburtstag. Ich habe ihr ein Buch und eine Karte gekauft. Am Abend habe ich ihr das Geschenk gegeben, und sie hat sich sehr gefreut.
model.en: It was my sister's birthday last week. I bought her a book and a card. In the evening I gave her the present, and she was very happy.

tips: Keep the person before the thing when both are nouns: meiner Schwester ein Buch.
If you replace the thing with a pronoun, the pronoun comes first: Ich gebe es ihr.
Check the dative article before you speak. Saying ihrer Schwester instead of ihre Schwester is the whole difference between the cases.

sections.title: Common mistakes
sections.lede: Most errors come from giving the person the wrong case.

items.wrong: Ich gebe das Kind einen Apfel.
items.right: Ich gebe dem Kind einen Apfel.
items.why: The child receives the apple, so it stands in the dative: dem Kind.

items.wrong: Sie schenkt ihre Schwester ein Buch.
items.right: Sie schenkt ihrer Schwester ein Buch.
items.why: The recipient is dative, and die Schwester becomes ihrer Schwester.
zeigen takes a dative person, so mich becomes mir.
When two pronouns meet, the accusative comes before the dative.
